Or does it feel more like a persistent depression that is not tied to reminders?\n\nPatient: It really feels much more like a constant, heavy depression that is always there. I don't have nightmares or find myself trying to avoid reminders of her; it's just this flat, empty feeling and joylessness that hasn't let up since a few months after the funeral.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?\n\nPatient: Yes, almost every day I catch myself thinking it would be better if I just didn't wake up. I’ve even pictured taking all my old pain pills at once so I could finally stop being a burden to everyone. It really scares me afterward when I have those thoughts, but they still come.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed any changes in your sleep, appetite, energy, or ability to concentrate since this started?\n\nPatient: My appetite is completely gone, and food just tastes like cardboard to me, so I have to force down a few bites of toast or soup. I also feel exhausted from the moment I wake up, like I've run a marathon, and even simple things like taking a shower wear me out. I just don't have any energy left.\n\nDoctor: Since your sister died, have you had intrusive memories, nightmares, flashbacks, or strong avoidance of reminders of what happened? Or is it mainly a persistent depressed mood and loss of interest that is present most days regardless of reminders?\n\nPatient: It is definitely the persistent depressed mood and complete loss of interest that fills almost every day. I don't really have flashbacks or nightmares about her passing, but rather a heavy, unrelenting sadness where nothing in life has any point anymore. It has been constant like this for over a year now.\n\nDoctor: Did your symptoms start within a few months of your sister’s death and have they stayed present most days for more than 2 weeks, or did they begin right away and mainly come and go in response to reminders of the loss?\n\nPatient: They started within a few months after my sister's funeral and have stayed with me almost constantly for over a year now. It isn't something that just comes and goes when I'm reminded of her; this heavy, joyless feeling is just there every single day.\n\nDoctor: Before your sister died, did you already have a period of depressed mood or loss of interest for at least two weeks, or did these symptoms only begin after her death?\n\nPatient: No, I never experienced anything like this before my sister passed away. I was very active with my church and loved my gardening, and I didn't have those sad feelings at all. It was only in the months after her funeral that this heavy depression and loss of interest started to develop.\n\nDoctor: Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people do not, or feeling like your thoughts are being controlled or that others are trying to harm you?\n\nPatient: Yes, at night when the house is quiet, I hear my sister clearly calling my name and telling me I'm a burden and should come with her. I also... I'm convinced some of the ladies from my church are watching me and working with the city and the hospital to take my house away.\n\nDoctor: Do you believe these voices or fears are definitely true, or do you ever recognize that they might be part of an illness or your mind playing tricks on you?\n\nPatient: I know deep down that my sister is gone, but when I hear her voice at night, it sounds so completely real and it just terrifies me. And as for the church ladies, I am absolutely certain they are watching me and trying to take my house—my daughter keeps telling me it's just my mind playing tricks, but I just can't believe her when it feels so real.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever heard voices or had beliefs that others were watching, controlling, or trying to harm you when you were not feeling depressed? Or do these experiences only happen during the times when your depression is at its worst?\n\nPatient: Usually they happen at the same time, but there was a spell last fall when my mood felt a bit more neutral and I wasn't crying so much. Even during those few weeks, I still heard my sister's voice calling to me at night and remained convinced that the church women were watching me. So those experiences kept going even when the depression lifted a little.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had the hearing your sister’s voice or the belief that people were watching you at times when you were not depressed at all, or did those experiences only happen during your depressive episodes?\n\nPatient: Yes, last fall there was a period of several weeks where my mood felt a bit more neutral and I wasn't crying as much. Even though the deep depression wasn't as heavy then, I still clearly heard my sister's voice at night and believed the church women were watching me. So those experiences did happen even when I wasn't feeling as depressed.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had the hearing your sister’s voice or the belief that people were watching you at times when you were not depressed at all, or did those experiences only happen during your depressive episodes?\n\nPatient: Yes, last fall there was a period of a few weeks where my mood felt a bit more neutral and I wasn't crying as much. But even though the deep sadness lifted a bit, I still clearly heard my sister calling me at night and felt certain those church women were watching me. It’s just so exhausting that those things didn't go away.\n\nDoctor: Have the voices or beliefs that people are watching you ever continued for at least 2 weeks when you were not depressed at all, or do they only happen when your depression is present?\n\nPatient: Yes, last fall there was a period of several weeks where my mood felt a bit more neutral and I wasn't crying as much. But even though the deep sadness lifted for that time, I still clearly heard my sister calling me at night and felt certain those church women were watching me. So yes, those things definitely continued for weeks even when the depression wasn't really there.\n\nDoctor: Have the voices or beliefs that people are watching you ever continued for at least 2 weeks when you were not depressed at all, or do they only happen when your depression is present?\n\nPatient: Yes, during that time last fall, my mood was much more neutral for several weeks and I wasn't crying or feeling deeply depressed. Yet, even without the depression, I still heard my sister's voice every night and felt sure the church ladies were watching me. So yes, those things definitely continued on their own for more than two weeks.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you had the voices or beliefs that people were watching you, but you did not feel depressed at all?\n\nPatient: Yes, that's what happened last fall when my mood felt a little more neutral and I wasn't crying as much for a few weeks. Even though I didn't feel depressed then, I still heard my sister's voice at night and felt sure the church women were watching me.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you heard voices or believed people were watching you, but you did not feel depressed at all?\n\nPatient: Yes, last fall there was a period of several weeks where my mood felt much more neutral and I wasn't feeling depressed or crying at all. Even though the sadness was gone during those weeks, I still clearly heard my sister's voice at night and felt convinced the church women were watching me.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you heard voices or believed people were watching you, but you did not feel depressed at all?\n\nPatient: Yes, last fall there was a stretch of several weeks where my mood felt much more neutral and I didn't feel depressed or cry at all. Even though the sadness had lifted during those weeks, I still clearly heard my sister's voice at night and remained convinced the church women were watching me.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you heard voices or believed people were watching you, but you did not feel depressed at all?\n\nPatient: Yes, that's right. Last fall there was a period of several weeks where my mood was completely neutral and I didn't feel depressed, but I still heard my sister's voice and believed the church women were watching me. It lasted for about a month like that.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you heard voices or believed people were watching you, but you did not feel depressed at all?\n\nPatient: Yes, as I mentioned, last fall there was a period of a few weeks where my mood felt much more neutral and I wasn't crying or feeling depressed. Even without the sadness, I still clearly heard my sister calling my name at night and remained convinced the church women were watching me.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you heard voices or believed people were watching you, but you did not feel depressed at all?\n\nPatient: Yes, last fall there was a stretch of about three or four weeks where I didn't feel depressed or cry at all. Yet, during those weeks, I still heard my sister calling me at night and felt certain the church ladies were watching me.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had hallucinations or strong beliefs that people were watching or trying to harm you for at least 2 weeks when you were not depressed at all?"

========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
Yes, last fall there was a period of about a month where my mood felt much more neutral and I wasn't feeling depressed. But even without the depression, I still clearly heard my sister's voice at night and remained convinced that the church women were watching me.
